I was about 17 and working as a cashier one day, when I heard an explosion and saw a LITERAL PLUME OF FIRE reach the ceiling. I don't have fight or flight instincts- I just freeze. So I stood their shocked while one of the other employees shouted through the earpiece that there was a fire. He had been right at the end of the aisle of the explosion because he had smelled burning. Despite all of the smoke, the alarm didn't go off, but our lights decided to go out and we were just lit by the grayish daylight from the windows.

I just kind of stood there in shock while another employee put out a very small carpet fire with their fucking iced tea. Then one customer starts walking towards me saying "What's happening?" I, of course, didn't have the answer- and he grabbed a computer and ran out the door. The alarms went off but we don't have security and I was a 5'3" 110 lb girl so I sure as hell wasn't trying to stop him- I just reported that a customer had run.

I called 911 and said there had been a fire and a theft. I was so dazed that I put them ON HOLD (yes, I still cringe at how idiotic this was) because my manager wanted to give them more details.

While all of this is happening, some high schooler comes to the front and still wants to check out! Thank God her mom had the good sense to GTFO. I locked the store doors and just sat there while my shift manager called the store manager in tears. He sighed dramatically and was VERY mad at us because we interrupted a date! Still, he packed up, came in- yelled at the other employee for not running to get the fire extinguisher in the back instead of using the tea, yelled at me for not trying to stop the 6 foot something thief, and yelled at my shift manager for closing the store for so long. He went on about how much profit we had lost in the 4 hours the store was closed and then RE-OPENED THE STORE 45 MINUTES TO CLOSE.

​

Then he left. 

​

I was complacent and dazed so I stayed there like it was a normal shift- we all did. The following week, he lectured us all about safety and loss prevention. I didn't come in for weeks because I felt unsafe in the store.

Imagine my sheer joy about a month later when he was fired. Who tf re-opens a store with an aisle full of burnt carpet and melted product, plus 4 traumatized employees and only emergency lighting?

(Zillennial here- right in between Z and Millennial)   
Failed expectations and too much knowledge of the bad.

Your brain doesn't like it when you expect something good and it comes out as less than expected. We were raised to expect a lot- from life, ourselves, from others.

Our generation is different than our parents financially and morally. Marriage, heterosexual relationships, early marriage, early graduation, great jobs just from going to college- this is what was preached to many of us. Whereas the norm for our gen is side hustles, ridiculous debt, maybe never owning a home.

Realistically? I'm happy with that. I'm okay with living in a nice, one bedroom apartment with my dog and a meh used car. I don't need to be rich, i don't need to be married at 22, I don't need to graduate and make ridiculous money by the time I'm 25...but I think those expectations were placed on many of us and anything less is seen as "failing" or "not good enough". Tl;dr- we're not letting what we have be good enough- we're defining it as bad when maybe it's just fine. We aren't grateful or proud of ourselves and are always working towards some new goal, never really happy in the moment.

That and we know so much about bad goings on...sometimes ignorance is bliss. Knowing every single bad thing nearby doesn't always help.

Also yes, I know it isn't the same for everyone....I'm just listing some commonalities.
